pan_estimate.basis: rubber centre and width read on centre-field frames, plate front edge of the same frame

hop2.source: tilt = mean sin(tilt) from the batter's-box 6-ft depth readings; pan = mean from rubber readings (0 when none were read); nominal mitt depth 2.5 ft behind the plate front (assumed, not measured)

hop1_front_edge_noise.definition: rms(A - B)/sqrt(2) over both ends and both coordinates

pan.basis: mean lateral offset of the plate's back-edge midpoint vs front-edge midpoint over all M1 plate quads

pan_from_rubber.method: session (Claude) visual reading of the pitching rubber centre vs the plate front-edge centre on two gridded decision frames; 60.5 ft lever
pan_from_rubber.camera_distance_basis: rubber width 84 px for 24 in vs plate scale 36.4 px/ft: D/(D-60.5) = 1.15
pan_from_rubber.note: a nearer point on the mound-plate line shifting image-left means deeper points shift image-right (more negative plate_x); the implied term is far smaller than the measured x offset

tilt.basis: batter's box front/back chalk lines 6 ft apart, lateral scale from the same frame's plate front edge (M1 corners)

lateral_check.caveat: readers marked line centres; chalk lines are 2-4 in wide, so a +/-0.1-0.17 ft convention term is included; transform-only, on-plane, no depth parallax

overlay_check.conclusion: the overlay's width matches the plate width and its height reproduces the per-pitch feed zone height under the lateral px/ft scale, so the vertical scale equals the lateral scale; the overlay sits a constant offset above the plate-front ground line (it is drawn at a deeper point of the plate), so its edges are not used as an origin

chosen_offset_seconds.definition: offset of the first ball-in-mitt frame relative to release_seconds + plateTime (the catch-time residual of the manual release annotation)

error_definition: 2-D rms over called pitches of (hops 1-2 with the calibrated matrix applied to the ball/pocket on the first frame with the ball in the mitt, A/B reader mean) minus (Statcast trajectory at y = -1.0 ft, i.e. 2.4 ft behind the plate front); computed on the human-verified pitches when at least min_pitches were confirmed, otherwise on all used pitches; the parallax term is removed for the nominal 2.5 ft depth, so a residual mean offset reflects the true catch depth differing from that assumption plus reader noise; pixel readings are assistant visual estimates (a person confirmed them on a montage, not re-marked them); development game (docs/results/mlb_p0/intent_eval_plan_v0.json)
